newsitem.title: UK: UK negative equity falls in Q3 1996 - Woolwich.
newsitem.headline: UK negative equity falls in Q3 1996 - Woolwich.

text.p: The number of British households blighted by negative equity fell by 65,000 in the third quarter of 1996 and now totals 475,000, the Woolwich Building Society said on Thursday.
That means the number of households with properties worth less than the value of mortgages taken out on them has dropped below half a million for the first time since mid-1990.
The Woolwich said a 0.6 percent rise in national house prices between the second and third quarters was largely responsible for the drop.

"The significant fall in the number of households with negative equity this year is a further sign we are now experiencing a sustained housing market recovery," said John Stewart, group chief executive of the Woolwich Building Society.
The report said almost 70 percent of households with negative equity are located in the south of England.
Overall, the number of blighted households has dropped by 685,000 this year, due to a combination of a six percent rise in national house prices and capital repayments by borrowers.

"Evidence that the broader economy is picking up should underpin further improvements in confidence which, together with the lowest mortgage rates and the most affordable housing for a generation, is expected to ensure that the recovery continues," Stewart said.
